newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan denies giving $4.3 million to Sao Tome.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan denies giving $4.3 million to Sao Tome.

text.p: Taiwan on Saturday denied it had begun funding Sao Tome and Principe, with which it recently established official relations in a diplomatic tug-of-war with rival China.

"Reports about Sao Tome already receiving US$4.3 million from us are inaccurate. Until now, we have yet to give it even one cent," Roy Wu, spokesman of Taiwan's foreign ministry, said in a news briefing.

He said Taiwan would offer financial aid to Sao Tome to help it develop its economy, but provision of such aid would be conducted according to a set plan, and would need approval from Taiwan's parliament.
Sao Tome officials said on Friday the African republic had received a pledge from Taiwan to provide aid totalling $30 million over the next decade after deciding to establish ties with Taipei.
Sao Tome Foreign Minister Homero Salvaterra visited Taiwan early in May, where he received $4.3 million as a first instalment, the officials said.
Sao Tome President Miguel Trovoada on Thursday issued a decree confirming the opening of diplomatic ties with Taiwan effective from May 7 despite a parliamentary vote opposing the move.
China, a bitter rival of Taiwan since a civil war split the two in 1949, has accused the island of trying to use money to buy international relations.
It has warned other countries against forging ties with Taipei, saying Taiwan is a rebel-held province of China ineligible to foreign relations.

Since wresting China's U.N. seat from the Nationalists in the 1970s, Beijing has won the recognition of most world governments. Taipei today has diplomatic links with only 30 states, most of them small, poor and dependent on its financial largesse.
President Trovoada justified his decision to open ties with Taiwan by saying Sao Tome desperately needed financial aid.

Sao Tome and Principe, a former Portuguese colony located 200 km (125 miles) off Gabon, is one of the world's poorest countries and is heavily dependent on foreign aid. The islands' population is 127,000.
